meta.source: Manufacturer household-size sizing guides: American Water Heater Residential Product Catalog (Residential Water Heater Selection Guide), Rheem (What Size Gas Water Heater Do I Need for My Home?, 2026) and A. O. Smith (What Size Water Heater Is Right for You?)
meta.notes: Rules of thumb that size by the number of people. They disagree with each other because each assumes its own habits and fuel; the peak-hour method (data/peak-hour-demand.json) is the primary method and these tables are shown next to it as a cross-check. American gives a first hour rating (FHR) requirement; Rheem (gas tanks) and A. O. Smith give tank volume. Opened and copied 2026-11-13.

american.label: American Water Heater
american.source: American Water Heater, Residential Product Catalog: Residential Water Heater Selection Guide, Simple Tank Type Sizing (First Hour Rating requirements by family size)
american.note: Move up one level for a high-demand home: more than two full baths, teenagers, or an oversize tub.

rheem.label: Rheem (gas tanks)
rheem.source: Rheem, What Size Gas Water Heater Do I Need for My Home? (Recommended Tank Sizes by Household Size)
rheem.note: For 5 or more people Rheem suggests 75 gallons or a tankless unit.

example.label: Two showers, one load of laundry and kitchen use

aosmith.label: A. O. Smith
aosmith.source: A. O. Smith, What Size Water Heater Is Right for You? (storage tank size guide by family size)
aosmith.note: Tank volume for any fuel; A. O. Smith also says to choose a unit whose first hour rating equals or slightly exceeds your peak-hour demand.
